_comment: mouse.json with the wavelet backend instead of the short-time Fourier transform. Use it when you need timing that a fixed 2 s window smears -- brief REM bouts, transitions, microarousals. It costs far more memory and time: the scalogram gives one column per sample rather than one per epoch, so score a window rather than a whole 24 h recording, or resample first. Start from mouse.json; reach for this only if the spectrogram is losing something you can see.

EEG._comment: freq_resolution is the frequency step in Hz, and replaces binsize: the wavelet's window scales with frequency instead of being fixed. Rows = (max_freq - min_freq) / freq_resolution, so halving this doubles the memory. f0 sets the wavelet's cycles (higher = sharper in frequency, blunter in time); exp_corr reweights across scales, 0 leaves it alone. time_smooth is in seconds and is applied inside the transform.

EMG._comment: Coarser in frequency than the EEG: this band is collapsed to a single power trace, so resolution buys nothing and costs memory.

steps._comment: gmm rather than the hdbscan mouse.json uses. hdbscan chooses its own number of clusters from a density scale, and that scale is set by hdbscan_min_cluster_size in *points* -- which here is one per sample rather than one per epoch, hundreds of times more. At mouse.json's 300 it fragments a night into dozens of clusters, and any cluster stage_order does not name is left unscored. A fixed n_clusters does not have that failure mode. If you prefer hdbscan, raise hdbscan_min_cluster_size in the same proportion as the bin rate.
steps.name: split_sleep
